extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house IP counsel, and PTAB practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance summarizing district-court treatments of stays, IPR/PGR estoppel, collateral estoppel, admissibility of PTAB/ex parte proceedings, attorneys' fees under §285, and related procedural issues in patent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay factors (simplification, prejudice, stage of case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts weigh whether a stay will simplify issues, whether it will prejudice the non-moving party, and the stage of the case (e.g., claim construction, discovery, trial date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly applied: stay denied where lack of simplification or prejudice to plaintiff; stay granted where potential simplification and lack of prejudice. Examples: stay denied when defendant challenged only some patents and discovery was complete with trial soon (WSOU v. F5); stay granted where stage, simplification, and lack of prejudice favored it (MicroPairing Techs. v. Am. Honda).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-institution stay skepticism — need to show institution likely
rubrics_metrics.description: When seeking a stay before the PTAB decides institution, a movant must make a persuasive showing that institution is likely; otherwise simplification is speculative and weighs against a stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied pre-institution stay because defendant failed to explain why institution was likely, making any simplification speculative (MZ Audio Sciences v. Sony; Skillz Platform pre-institution denial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and diligence in filing IPR petitions (affects stay and prejudice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Late filing of IPR petitions (e.g., filed weeks before Markman or long after discovery) weighs against a stay and may be prejudicial to the non-movant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts noted petitions filed shortly before Markman and after fact discovery supported denial of stay (WSOU v. F5). Delay in seeking reexamination requests can justify lifting a stay (MG Freesites v. Scorpcast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitor relationship weighs against staying litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the parties are competitors, courts may view the prejudice factor as weighing against a stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if other factors favor a stay, the parties’ status as competitors can tip the balance against a stay (Skillz Platform Inc. v. AviaGames; Smith Sport Optics reopened where parties were competitors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial stays: stay only patents with instituted IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may stay litigation only as to patents for which the PTAB has instituted IPRs and continue litigation for patents where institution was denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court stayed three patents subject to instituted IPRs but did not stay the fourth where institution was denied (Aortic Innovations v. Edwards Lifescis.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prejudice assessment includes patent expiry, practice, injunctive relief, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Expiration of the patents, whether plaintiff practices the patents, whether plaintiff seeks injunctive relief, and relative sizes/resources of parties are relevant to prejudice analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration and lack of practice/injunctive relief indicate less prejudice (MicroPairing Techs.); small plaintiff vs large defendant resources can show prejudice from a stay (Aortic Innovations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel under 35 U.S.C. § 315(e) requires a final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory IPR estoppel (35 U.S.C. § 315(e)(2)) applies only where the PTAB issued a final written decision; denied where PTAB did not institute or issue a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No statutory estoppel where PTAB declined to institute (inMusic Brands v. Roland); estoppel invoked only post-final written decision (Innovative Memory Sys. estoppel example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel can extend to non-petitioned combinations involving an instituted reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If PTAB institutes and issues a final written decision as to a ground involving a reference, combinations that involve that reference but were not specifically petitioned can be estopped as non-petitioned grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court held that Pandit (instituted and decided) estopped Pandit-by-itself and combinations of Pandit with other references as estopped non-petitioned grounds (Arendi v. LG Elecs.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel does not apply to prior-art products even if cumulative to IPR references
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of statutory interpretation, IPR estoppel does not cover prior-art products, even if those products are cumulative to references asserted in the IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court refused to extend IPR estoppel to prior-art products and aligned with district courts adhering to statutory language (Chemours Co. v. Daikin Indus.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel for a reference if it could have reasonably been raised (searchability standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may estop a party from later relying on a reference if it could have been reasonably located and raised in the IPR (e.g., via straightforward CPC-class searches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant estopped for grounds based on a U.S. patent that could have been found by running straightforward searches on the CPC class (Innovative Memory Sys. v. Micron Tech.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral estoppel requires claims to be 'materially the same' and identity of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Collateral estoppel may bar asserting claims materially the same as those held unpatentable in IPR/reexamination if ordinary issue-preclusion elements are met; differences in claim limitations or differing claim construction standards can prevent estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied estoppel for most asserted claims because they included additional limitations distinguishing them from PTAB-held claims; but where an asserted claim recited the same features as a PTAB-unpatentable claim, estoppel applied (XR Commc’ns v. D-Link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-patent collateral estoppel from inter partes reexamination final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A final decision in inter partes reexamination can have preclusive effect across patents if issue-preclusion elements are satisfied and there are no special circumstances rendering estoppel inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court found reexamination final decisions precluded certain invalidity grounds against a third patent because issues and parties were sufficiently the same and the reexamination provided a full and fair opportunity to litigate (SynQor v. Vicor).

rubrics_metrics.name: District court not bound by PTAB denials of institution when considering invalidity in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A PTAB decision to deny institution is non-controlling in district court; a reasonable jury may still find invalidity by clear and convincing evidence based on the same references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied summary judgment of no invalidity despite PTAB denials because the district court is not bound by those decisions and reasonable expert testimony could support invalidity (Altria v. R.J. Reynolds Vapor).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB proceedings and ex parte reexamination evidence may be excluded from jury trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may grant motions in limine to exclude evidence of USPTO/PTAB proceedings from jury trial where their relevance is substantially outweighed by the risk of unfair prejudice and jury confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court excluded both IPR and ex parte reexamination evidence on grounds of potential jury confusion and unfair prejudice (Trustees Univ. Pa. v. Eli Lilly).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR-related attorney’s fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 generally unavailable for PTO proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A court held that IPR proceedings are not part of the patent infringement “case” under § 285 when the party voluntarily sought IPR, so attorney fees incurred during IPR are unavailable under § 285 and alleged misconduct during the IPR cannot support an exceptional-case finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sherwood Sensing Sol’ns v. Henny Penny: court declined to include IPR fees or IPR misconduct in § 285 exceptional-case analysis because the IPR was voluntarily sought and not part of the infringement 'case.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential infringement contentions produced for PTAB use limited in district court
rubrics_metrics.description: Production of confidential infringement contentions to the PTAB does not authorize use of those contentions in PTAB filings absent agreement; district court may prohibit using those contentions in PTAB filings even if PTAB ordered production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court found no protective-order violation but prohibited defendants from using plaintiff’s confidential infringement contentions in PTAB filings (Parkervision v. TCL Indus.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial notice of IPR statements can doom inconsistent infringement allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a plaintiff's infringement allegations contradict its prior statements in an IPR (e.g., disavowal of a claim construction), a court may take judicial notice of those IPR statements and dismiss infringement claims for failure to plead plausibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff dismissed where it had disavowed a claim construction in a prior IPR and then alleged infringement based on that disavowed construction (Grecia Estate Holdings v. Meta Platforms).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB denial for lack of particularity (scattershot petitions) not dispositive in court
rubrics_metrics.description: Board denials of PGRs for lack of particularity do not bind district courts; courts may deny motions for summary judgment of no invalidity based on rejected petitions because the Board's reasoning and non-institution are non-controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied summary judgment of no invalidity where PTAB denied PGRs as 'scattershot'—the district court is not bound to adopt the Board’s non-institution rationale (DynaEnergetics v. Hunting Titan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may lift or refuse to extend a stay based on its original terms (duration limited to IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stay was granted only for the duration of the IPR, the court may reopen the case after the PTAB’s final written decision even if appeal is pending; parties wanting an extended stay should request it initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court reopened case after PTAB final decision despite pending appeal because the stay had been limited to the IPR's duration (Targus Int’l v. Group III Int’l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of trial date can prejudice IPR petitioners and justify denial
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff’s attempt to accelerate trial before resolution of IPR institution/final decision can prejudice defendant because PTAB might deny petitions based on an accelerated schedule and depriving summary judgment briefing can cause substantial prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied plaintiff’s requested trial acceleration and cancellation of summary judgment briefing where an IPR institution decision (if instituted) would yield a final written decision after the proposed accelerated date and defendant would be prejudiced (Skills Platform v. AviaGames).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of motions to stay pending third-party IPRs if limited simplification and undue prejudice risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to stay litigation pending third-party IPRs can be denied where the stay would offer limited simplification (not all asserted claims challenged) and would unduly prejudice the patentee (loss of enforcement opportunity, evidence loss).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts declined to stay for third-party IPRs when simplification was limited and prejudice significant (mCom IP v. Bank of America; mCom IP v. Cisco).

rubrics_metrics.name: No IPR estoppel or common-law estoppel where no IPR instituted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the PTAB declined to institute any IPRs, neither statutory IPR estoppel under §315(e)(2) nor common-law preclusion will apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court granted motion to strike affirmative defense asserting estoppel where PTAB declined to institute (inMusic Brands v. Roland).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims can survive estoppel applied to parent independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff asserting dependent claims that add limitations to an independent claim held unpatentable in IPR may nevertheless be allowed to argue lack of the limitation in prior art because PTAB's lower standard may not preclude differing district-court outcomes for dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied motion to estop plaintiff from arguing that prior art lacked a limitation for dependent claims even though independent claims were held unpatentable in IPR (IOENGINE LLC v. PayPal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for Rule 12(f) motions unaffected by PTAB timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to strike under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(f) must be filed within the 21-day window irrespective of later PTAB proceedings; PTAB final decisions do not revive or extend that deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied untimely motion to strike inequitable conduct defense despite PTAB decisions because the 21-day deadline had long passed (Chervon (HK) Ltd. v. One World Techs.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may refuse to exclude system art based on IPR stipulations when publications may not fully describe systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant's prior IPR stipulations that it would not advance certain grounds in district court do not necessarily bar the defendant from asserting system references whose publicly available publications may not fully describe relevant system features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court denied plaintiff's motion in limine to preclude defendant's system art where it was not clear that the related publications fully described all relevant features (United Servs. Auto. Ass’n. PNC Bank N.A.).
